text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- Six Reform Party ministers announced in a public letter their intention to leave the government and the party assembly will discuss leaving the ruling coalition today. The Coalition Party would start negotiations over a new coalition only after the Reform Party ministers have formally resigned, leading party member Mart Siimann said.
- Norwegian Prime Minister Thornbjorn Jagland was satisfied with his two-day visit to Tallinn, predicting increased investments by Norway in Estonia and visa-free travel in a year.
- Estonian and Russian delegations reached agreement on simplified border crossing regulations for residents of the border areas.
- The joint Baltic unit, the Baltic Battalion, was a suitable model for developing WEU implementation force, Estonian Defence Minister Andrus Oovel said on his return from a WEU meeting.
- Norway's civil defence force delivered eight truck-loads of used rescue equipment as a present to the Estonian Rescue Department.
- The Reform Party spent 1.6 million kroons on its campaign at the local council elections, a million kroons of which was spent in Tallinn.
- The International Advertising Association (IAA) is holding a meeting on November 25 in Tallinn, to form a sub-organisation in Estonia.
